svg.aria-label: Diagram: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling instance maintenance policies. A policy sets a minimum and maximum healthy percentage that applies to every event that replaces an instance in the group. The console offers three options: launch before terminating, where a new instance must be provisioned first before an existing instance can be terminated; terminate and launch, where new instances are provisioned at the same time existing ones are terminated; and a custom policy with its own minimum and maximum range. Without a policy the group uses per-event defaults, and these are not uniform: health check failure, instance refresh and maximum instance lifetime all default to terminate and launch, while rebalancing defaults to launch before terminating and may exceed the group's size limits by up to 10 percent of its maximum capacity, or by up to 10 percent of the desired capacity when Capacity Rebalancing is enabled. Three documented situations continue to default to terminate and launch regardless of the policy, so group capacity might be less than the policy's lower threshold: an instance terminating unexpectedly such as through human action, Amazon EC2 rebooting stopping or retiring an instance as part of a scheduled event before a replacement can launch, and a Spot Instance being forcibly terminated after the Spot Service initiates an interruption, which carries a two-minute interruption notice. Auto Scaling may have advance notice of these events, and with Capacity Rebalancing enabled the group tries to launch new Spot Instances before existing ones are interrupted, but it cannot guarantee a replacement is in service before the termination, so the policy's lower threshold can be exceeded if instances are interrupted before the new instances have launched. Four places can set the percentages and the precedence runs from instance refresh preferences, through the instance maintenance policy on the group, to the launchBeforeTerminate account setting, which applies a minimum of 100 and a maximum of 110 when nothing more specific is set, and finally to the per-event defaults. Valid values are 0 to 100 percent for the minimum healthy percentage and 100 to 200 percent for the maximum. An instance counts toward the minimum only after it completes its first health check and the specified warmup time passes, so the default instance warmup prevents instances being counted before they are ready. With a warm pool the percentages are applied separately to the group and the warm pool, so a minimum of 90 and maximum of 120 against a desired capacity of 100 and a warm pool of 10 gives 90 to 120 instances in the group and 9 to 12 in the warm pool. A policy only applies to instance maintenance events and does not prevent the group being manually or automatically scaled. Launch before terminate runs one additional instance for a short time during each replacement, and if capacity for the replacement cannot be obtained the original instance is kept in service and retried. With a targeted Capacity Reservation referenced by a specific Capacity Reservation ID, the freed slot does not reclaim the replacement instance, so one instance keeps running as On-Demand capacity while one reserved slot stays unused.
svg.title: The policy sets a floor that three events ignore
svg.text: One minimum, and three events allowed to go under it.
“Your group’s capacity might be less than the lower threshold of your instance maintenance policy.”
The three that keep terminating first, whatever the policy says
An instance terminates unexpectedly — “for example, because of human action”
EC2 reboots, stops or retires an instance on a scheduled event, before the replacement launches
A Spot Instance is forcibly terminated after an interruption — two-minute notice
Auto Scaling may see all three coming. What it cannot guarantee is a replacement in service before they land.
NO POLICY: DEFAULTS DISAGREE
health check failure terminate and launch
instance refresh terminate and launch
max instance lifetime terminate and launch
rebalancing LAUNCH BEFORE TERM.
Rebalancing may overshoot by 10% of maximum
capacity — or of desired, with Cap. Rebalancing.
FOUR PLACES, ONE ORDER
1. instance refresh preferences
2. the group’s maintenance policy
3. launchBeforeTerminate account setting
4. the per-event defaults, left
The account setting carries min 100, max 110 — and
one extra instance for a short time, each replacement.
THE TWO RANGES
minimum healthy 0 - 100%
maximum healthy 100 - 200%
They meet at one value. Capacity during a
replacement is a band, and these are its edges.
WARM POOLS COUNT SEPARATELY
group desired 100 → 90 to 120
pool size 10 → 9 to 12
Min 90%, max 120%, applied twice. The group is
replaced before the warm pool is touched.
Launch before terminate plus a targeted reservation, referenced by ID
“The freed slot does not reclaim the instance. One instance keeps running as On-Demand capacity
while one reserved slot stays unused.”
Paying twice for one instance of capacity. Use an open reservation, or a resource group ARN.
An instance counts toward the minimum only after its first health check AND the warmup time passes.
A policy applies to maintenance events only, and does not stop the group being scaled manually or automatically.
If replacement capacity cannot be found, the original instance stays in service and Auto Scaling retries.
